# P3 deploy-box runbook — env prefixes, URL vars and systemd units

The P3 restructure renamed workspaces, env prefixes, public URL variables and systemd units.
The repo half is committed; **the boxes are not**. Until these steps run, a redeploy brings
apps up with no env block — every `PREFIX__` lookup misses — and the renamed units do not exist.

Applies to the VPS (rutba.pk) and the LAN box (`rutba-nvr@192.168.0.46`). The LAN box keeps its
master env **off-git**, so it cannot be replaced wholesale — it must be rewritten in place.

> Do the env half and the unit half in the **same window**. An app whose unit was renamed but
> whose env was not will start and then fail every authenticated request.

## 1. Env prefixes and URL variables

23 env prefixes and 7 URL variables changed. Do **not** hand-write seds for this —
run the tool, which is what the local machine was converted with:

```bash
# dry run first — prints every key it would rename, exits 1 if any are pending
node scripts/js/rename-env-prefixes.js .env.production

# apply (writes .env.production.bak alongside)
node scripts/js/rename-env-prefixes.js .env.production --write
```

It applies the renames longest-prefix-first, so `RUTBA_WEB__` cannot chew `RUTBA_WEB_USER__`,
and it **refuses** any rename whose target key already exists rather than creating a duplicate
— which matters for `NEXT_PUBLIC_CORE_URL` → `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, since strapi already owns
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`. A refusal is printed, not silently skipped; resolve those two by hand.

Re-running on a converted file prints `already current` and exits 0, so it is safe in a deploy
script and can gate the step.

## 2. systemd units — 9 renamed

Stop and disable the old unit **before** enabling the new one, or both bind the same port and
the second fails to start.

| App | Old unit | New unit | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| strapi | `rutba_pos_strapi` | `rutba_strapi` | 4010 |
| storefront | `rutba_web` | `rutba_storefront` | 4000 |
| stock | `rutba_pos_stock` | `rutba_stock` | 4001 |
| pos | `rutba_pos_sale` | `rutba_pos` | 4002 |
| auth | `rutba_pos_auth` | `rutba_auth` | 4003 |
| portal | `rutba_web_user` | `rutba_portal` | 4004 |
| orders | `rutba_order_management` | `rutba_orders` | 4013 |
| control | `rutba_inventory` | `rutba_control` | 4017 |
| console | `rutba_admin` | `rutba_console` | 4022 |

```bash
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_pos_strapi
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_web
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_pos_stock
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_pos_sale
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_pos_auth
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_web_user
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_order_management
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_inventory
sudo systemctl disable --now rutba_admin
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_strapi
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_storefront
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_stock
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_pos
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_auth
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_portal
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_orders
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_control
sudo systemctl enable --now rutba_console
```

## 3. Verify

```bash
node scripts/js/rename-env-prefixes.js .env.production   # must print "already current"
systemctl list-units "rutba_*" --no-pager                # all NEW names, all active
curl -sf localhost:4020/api/health || echo FAIL          # core answers
```

An app that starts but 500s on every authenticated route almost always means its env block did
not resolve — check that its `PREFIX__PORT` uses the new prefix.
